The Premium- RMS will include a Navigation module, a Communication module for wireless connectivity to internet and can be powered by high efficient solar cells (over 28% efficiency). description: autonomIQ is a deep-tech startup emerging from TU Darmstadt, developing simplymill – an AI-driven software solution that automates and optimizes Computer-Aided Manufacturing (CAM) for metalworking industries. Our technology targets precision manufacturing in single and small-batch production, addressing a major bottleneck in industrial efficiency: the manual, time-intensive process of programming CNC machines. Within the space manufacturing domain (upstream), simplymill enables suppliers and OEMs to produce complex, high-precision metal components for satellites, propulsion systems, and structural assemblies faster, more accurately, and with fewer resources. By automating process planning and toolpath generation, our solution significantly reduces programming times, energy consumption, and production costs—crucial advantages in a sector defined by low volumes, high complexity, and extreme quality standards. autonomIQ’s innovation leverages AI and process data learning to achieve fully autonomous CAM planning, bringing a step-change in manufacturing productivity for the space industry and beyond.

description: Bitrezus is focusing on reducing the risk of cyberattacks against space assets, using a combination of embedded H/W and blockchain technology to create an extra level of security. We enable critical opcode consensus in real-time, among untrusted partners, for resilient and cyber-proof operation of both space and ground infrastructure. Current satellite systems were not designed with security in mind. They have weak encryption and use legacy systems that are not easily patched or updated. Additionally, existing cybersecurity solutions rely on terrestrial stations becoming a single point of failure and performance bottleneck and are hardly scalable due to their centralized nature. Based on reports, a cyber-attack on the Global Positioning System alone could cost the U.S. $1 billion a day.
